title: burst-credit-repooling-and-cost-to-serve-workbook
content:
Purpose: sketch a mid-sprint playbook for repooling burst credits, reassigning reserved GPU budget across product groups, and a lightweight cost-to-serve workbook that ties token-price scenarios to near-term hiring bands.

Context / motivation:
- Rapid growth in Q2 usage has burned through our planned burst credit pool faster than expected. Need a short-term protocol to avoid emergency commit and to flatten margin volatility across product verticals.
- This doc is a working workbook: rough numbers, quick heuristics, and concrete follow-ups for finance + infra + product to action in the next 10 business days.

High-level constraints / assumptions (callout):
- Baseline monthly committed GPU spend (reserved + dedicated) = $1.6M/mo.
- Current burst credit (pool) = $120k remaining (expected to exhaust in ~11 days at current burn).
- Weighted average cost per 1M tokens served (mix of fp16 + int8 + quant ops) = $18.50 (internal blended).
- On-prem/dedicated customers account for ~18% of token volume but ~28% of committed spend.
- Hiring freeze in effect for product/marketing; limited exceptions for infra/SRE and delegated permanent headcount for capacity-critical roles.

Quick scenarios (3-way):
1) Hold-and-prioritize (conservative):
   - Repool: reallocate 40% of remaining burst credits to Dedicated/Enterprise customers to maintain SLAs; 60% to hosted API.
   - Hiring: allow 2 infra/SRE hires this quarter only if they reduce spot cost by >5%/mo within 6 weeks (quantization/infra engineering).
   - Pricing action: no public price change; internal throttles applied to free-tier heavy customers.
   - Expected outcome: burn extended ~18 days; margin impact minimal but availability preserved for SLA customers.

2) Neutral redistribution (balanced):
   - Repool: temporary priority buckets by product (hosted-engineering 45%, dedicated 35%, optimize/ops 20%).
   - Hiring: 1 applied-ML engineer approved to push quantization profiling across top 10 models (expected 6% cost reduction within 8 weeks).
   - Pricing action: small commit to trial micro-slab price bump for new enrollments (A/B via Console feature flag).
   - Expected outcome: burn extended ~28 days; small revenue friction but reduces urgency to commit more capacity.

3) Aggressive cost-saver (short-term margin protection):
   - Repool: concentrate burst credits on highest-margin customers only (top 25% by revenue); self-serve customers get throttles and default caching enabled.
   - Hiring: pause most hiring; reallocate contractor budget to infra optimization sprints.
   - Pricing action: temporary surfacing of a short-term surcharge on on-demand heavy routes (>500k tokens/day).
   - Expected outcome: immediate reduction in per-day burn (~22%); higher churn risk on low-touch accounts.

Mini Workbook: headcount vs cost delta (rough bands)
- Hypothesis: each infra-engineer assigned to batching/quant roadmap can reduce token cost by ~0.8%–1.5%/mo depending on model mix.
- Quick table (estimates):
  - 0 hires: monthly token cost = $18.50/1M tokens (baseline)
  - 1 infra hire (focused on quant infra): delta = -1.1% -> $18.30
  - 2 infra hires (split infra + SRE): delta = -1.9% -> $18.14
  - 1 applied-ML engineer (prompt+quant profiling): delta = -1.4% -> $18.24
  - 1 finance analyst (pricing experiments): enables +$10k/mo in optimized coupon allocation (soft benefit)

Price shock table (what-if): effect on runway if price per 1M tokens drops/increases
- Baseline revenue (hosted) = $2.2M/mo at current price bands.
- Case A: price compression -10% -> revenue delta -$220k/mo; need to cut $120k/mo from ops to preserve runway.
- Case B: price increase +8% (narrow hard-to-change): revenue delta +$176k/mo; opportunity to fund 2 infra hires.
- Callout: elasticity unknown for >5% changes — run two quick A/Bs on low-risk routes first (JIRA-5032).

Channels for short-term mitigation (operational pieces)
- Enable per-route soft-limits on free and freemium accounts (Product Console flag).
- Burst credit repooling procedure (ops-runbook): finance marks pool; product flags per-customer priority; infra enforces token-limits and cache-first policy.
- Queue a small canary price A/B for non-SME customers: 2.5% bump on new signups for 2 weeks via feature flags (track churn).

Risks & tradeoffs
- Reprioritizing burst credits to enterprise risks edge-case SLA blips for smaller high-volume apps — mitigated by transparent comms and temporary credits.
- Price bumps create churn risk; small, targeted A/B mitigates but increases operational complexity.
- Hiring infra helps long-term but headcount lead time and ramp means limited immediate effect; contractors cheaper but lower long-term ROI.

Concrete next steps (owners + ETA)
- Priya: finalize repooling allocation spreadsheet and publish to Confluence (by 2026-05-17) -> linked artifact.
- Ethan: experiment tag for A/B price canary and route-level flagging in Console (ticket JIRA-5032) -> set up by 2026-05-13.
- Zara: draft outbound comms to top-25 enterprise customers explaining temporary burst prioritization (by 2026-05-14).
- Benji: quick cost model run to show effect of 1/2 infra hires vs immediate contractor sprints (by 2026-05-16).

Open questions / to validate
- How many customers will be impacted by soft-limits? Need a segment extraction from product analytics (Ethan).
- What is the expected elastic response if we apply a 2.5% price bump to new signups? Run 2-week test.
- Can quantization improvements be accelerated by shifting 20% of contractor budget? (Zara + Priya)

Notes to self / rough heuristics used:
- Treated token cost as blended across model mix; real workbook should break out by model class (chat vs embed vs rerank).
- Did not include regional pricing differences (APAC cheaper on spot GPUs) — next iteration.
- Keep this doc lightweight: aim to convert to a short sheet with formulas and a one-pager for Exec briefing if scenario 2 is chosen.

Attachments & quick references:
- Link: Confluence page (linked_artifacts) for longer repooling policy draft.
- Analysis stub: attached CSV (not in Drive yet) with per-customer daily token history for last 30 days (Ethan to upload).

Status: draft — looking for quick alignment. Feedback loop: respond in-thread on this doc or add comments in Confluence.
summary: working workbook: repooling burst credits, three scenarios (hold/neutral/aggressive), a headcount-to-cost mini-workbook, price shock what-if table, operational mitigations, owners and dates
